title: JUNK and MPC Race Wheels Compared: Voodoo, Road Reaper, Killer JUNK and Black Magic
thumbnail_text: Four race wheels. Which one suits you?

scenes.heading: JUNK and MPC Race Wheels Compared
scenes.sub: Voodoo, Road Reaper, Killer JUNK and Black Magic, side by side
scenes.narration: By the end of this guide, you will know which of four top race wheels suits your frame, your surface and the way you skate. We will compare the JUNK Voodoo, the JUNK Road Reaper, the Killer JUNK and the MPC Black Magic. Choosing a race wheel is one of the most personal decisions in inline speed skating. Two wheels can look almost the same. They can roll on the same 608 bearings and fit the same frame. Yet at race pace, they can feel completely different under your foot. The hardness figures, the construction details and the race results here all come from the product data for these wheels.

scenes.heading: What all four share
bullets: Sold as a set of eight
You need sixteen 608 bearings and spacers
Check the diameter your frame takes
scenes.narration: First, what all four wheels have in common. Each one is sold as a set of eight. That is a full set for a pair of four wheel inline speed frames. The wheels come on their own, with no bearings. So whichever you choose, you will also need sixteen 608 bearings and the right spacers. Before you order, confirm the wheel diameter your frame is built for. A 110 millimetre wheel needs a frame set up for a 110 wheel. Once that is settled, the real differences come down to three things. Hardness, hub design, and the character each brand builds into the urethane.

scenes.heading: Grip versus roll
scenes.narration: Here is the firmness scale. On the left is Firm, which gives the most grip. In the middle is XFirm, at 84 to 86A, which balances grip and roll. On the right is XXFirm, at 86 to 88A, which rolls the most. The rule is simple. Softer wheels grip more. Harder wheels roll faster on smooth, dry surfaces. But there is a catch. On hard, smooth, dry ground, a harder wheel can start to slip. That is why grip still matters there. The right pick depends on how smooth and dry your surface is.

scenes.heading: Sizes and compounds stocked
scenes.narration: Now, what is actually on the shelf, because this shapes your choice. A filled green circle means the size or compound is stocked. Every one of the four wheels comes in both XFirm and XXFirm, so you are never forced into one compound. Diameter is where they differ. The Voodoo and the Black Magic come in 90, 100 and 110 millimetres. That makes them the natural choice on a 3 by 90, 4 by 90 or 4 by 100 frame. They also suit a junior skater still moving up through sizes. The Road Reaper and the Killer JUNK are 110 millimetre only. So they suit skaters already on a full size 4 by 110 frame.

scenes.heading: JUNK Voodoo, the pure all rounder
bullets: No pigment in hub or urethane
scenes.narration: Let us start with the JUNK Voodoo. It is a pure performance race wheel, with no pigment in either the hub or the urethane. Nothing is added that could compromise the natural qualities of the materials. It runs a natural turbo hub that has been re engineered for efficiency. JUNK also moulds each wheel in a one cavity tool, rather than the usual four cavity approach. That means tighter quality control, and more consistency from wheel to wheel. On the ground, it is made for precise control through tight corners and strong speed on the straights, on both road and track. If you want a consistent, do it all race wheel, the Voodoo is a superb starting point.

scenes.heading: JUNK Road Reaper, the decorated racer
bullets: Proven up to ultra marathon distance
scenes.narration: Next is the JUNK Road Reaper, one of the most decorated wheels in inline speed skating. It is a 110 millimetre wheel, the standard large diameter for the sport. Its record at the top level is serious. It has won senior and junior men's 100 metre titles at the World Championships. A 100 metre world record was set on it. And on the distance side, it has won the American Triple Crown of marathon and ultra distance races, including an 87 mile ultra marathon. From flat out sprints to ultra distance, this wheel has done it. The XFirm grips more on hard, smooth, dry surfaces, and the XXFirm rolls faster for outright speed.

scenes.heading: Four wheels, what stands out
scenes.narration: Here is the quick comparison. The Voodoo stands out for its pigment free turbo hub and one cavity moulding. It is the all round race wheel. The Road Reaper is the decorated 110 millimetre racer, proven at every distance. The Killer JUNK has a stiffer natural hub, which gives extra momentum in the pack. It suits pack racing and sprints. And the Black Magic brings its Soft Heart, Hard Body build on a Black Turbo hub, for grip and roll together. Each wheel has its own hub and construction story. Each one earns its place for a slightly different reason.

scenes.heading: Killer JUNK, the stiffer hub
bullets: Evolution of a legendary race wheel
Momentum in points and elimination races
scenes.narration: The Killer JUNK is JUNK's evolution of a legendary race wheel. It takes a wheel that carried skaters to many victories and world championships, and improves on it. The headline change is a noticeably stiffer hub, along with several other tweaks over the previous model. Distance skaters report extra momentum through points and elimination races. Sprinters get an edge in the closing stages of the 1,000 metres. Like the Voodoo, it uses a natural hub with no added pigment, and the urethane stays in its raw form. It is 110 millimetre only. If you like the JUNK approach but want that stiffer hub feel for the pack and the finish line, this is the pick.

scenes.heading: MPC Black Magic, Soft Heart, Hard Body
bullets: Soft inner ring, harder outer body
scenes.narration: The MPC Black Magic takes a different engineering route. It is widely regarded as the most successful wheel in the sport. It broke the 300 metre world record and went under 24 seconds for the first time. At one World Championships, it won more podium places than all other wheel brands combined. What sets it apart is MPC's patented technology, known as Soft Heart, Hard Body. A softer inner ring sits inside a harder outer layer of urethane. The soft heart lets the wheel flex for grip. The hard body keeps it rolling fast and lasting long. It sits on a stiffer Black Turbo hub, which adds roll and response.

scenes.heading: Which race wheel should you buy?
scenes.narration: So, which one should you buy? Work through four steps. Frame size first, then surface, then discipline, then feel. Frame size narrows the field fastest. On a 4 by 110 frame, all four wheels are open to you. On a 3 by 90, 4 by 90 or 4 by 100 frame, you are choosing between the Voodoo and the Black Magic. Next is surface. On a hard, smooth, dry track or road, XFirm gives you grip while still rolling well. That makes it the sensible default for most Indian rinks and road circuits. If you skate flat out on very smooth, dry ground and chase top speed, XXFirm rolls fastest.

scenes.heading: What a set of eight needs
scenes.narration: One last practical point. This diagram shows one foot, with four wheels on the frame. Each wheel takes two 608 bearings, with a spacer in the middle. A set of eight wheels covers both feet. So you need sixteen 608 bearings in total, plus the spacers. Plan for those when you order. And once your wheels are on, rotate them regularly. It keeps the wear even and makes a set last longer. How long a set lasts depends on your weight, your surface and how often you rotate.

scenes.heading: Trust your frame, your surface and your feel
scenes.sub: Full guide at livelica.com, link in the description
scenes.narration: Any of these four wheels will serve a serious skater well. The Voodoo is the pure, consistent all rounder. The Road Reaper is the decorated racer for every distance. The Killer JUNK adds a stiffer hub for pack racing and sprints. And the Black Magic brings its Soft Heart, Hard Body layering. The differences are real but fine. So trust your frame, your surface and your feel. The full guide is on the LiveLica blog, with every size and compound laid out. The link is in the description.
